teams.heading: Jake White opens Fiji reign with 34-28 win over Japan in Tokyo
teams.body: Jake White's first Test in charge ended in a 34-28 win over Japan in Tokyo, the first step of his Fiji reign. Both sides scored three first-half tries, but visiting replacement Ben Volavola settled it, kicking two penalties after the break. Fiji were briefly reduced to 14 men when Motikai Murray was yellow-carded in the 35th minute, a card later upgraded to red. The win avenged the 20-15 Pacific Nations Cup final defeat a month earlier and sets up November's Nations Championship Tests against France, Ireland and Italy.

lead.why: A fresh result, and the first Test of Jake White's Fiji reign, is a bigger story than the older White coverage already run.

teams.heading: Jack van Poortvliet signs multi-year Leicester deal, keeping England's scrum-half in place
teams.body: England scrum-half Jack van Poortvliet has signed a new multi-year deal with Leicester Tigers, BBC Sport reports. The 25-year-old has made 118 first-team appearances since graduating from the club's academy in 2019 and has played 27 times for England. He missed the 2023 World Cup after an ankle injury in a warm-up game, and he has an England contract for 2026-27. "I love playing rugby here," he told the club website. "It was a pretty easy decision to stay."

lead.why: A fresh, sourced England squad story about a current international scrum-half, with a clear event (a new contract) rather than opinion or hopeful speculation.

teams.heading: Jeremy Ward, South African-born Stade Français centre, named in France's 42-man squad
teams.body: Stade Français centre Jeremy Ward is in Fabien Galthié's 42-player squad for the Nations Championship, named on Wednesday, according to AFP. The South African-born player will not be eligible to play for France until next year, just before the World Cup in Australia. He is one of several players called up to fill gaps in an injury-hit squad, alongside Stade Français teammate Tani Vili. France face Fiji before South Africa in Paris on 13 November.

teams.heading: Andy Farrell names 36-man Ireland squad for the November internationals
teams.body: Andy Farrell has named a 36-man squad for Ireland's November internationals, the group that will face Argentina in Round four of the Nations Championship. It follows the 21-40 defeat to New Zealand in Round three, and The 42 Rugby Weekly is breaking down the talking points from the selection. The same week brings a blockbuster Leinster-Munster clash in Dublin.

teams.heading: Italy's last five games yield one win and four defeats
teams.body: Italy have won one of their last five games, and that single win sits furthest back: the sequence, most recent first, reads L L L L W. Four straight defeats now make up the current run, and the most recent of them was a 57-10 loss to Australia. The next fixture is Italy v South Africa in Round 4 of the Nations Championship.

teams.heading: Scotland's unprecedented Nations Championship squad depth could force big-name omissions
teams.body: The Scotsman reports that Scotland's squad depth for the Nations Championship is unprecedented, and that it could lead to several big-name omissions. Those selection calls come after a 33-17 win over Fiji in Round 3, with New Zealand next up in Round 4. Scotland have won two and lost one of their three matches, scoring 108 points and conceding 97.

lead.why: It is the only new men's national-team item in the shortlist, and it concerns Scotland's own squad selection.

teams.heading: Taulupe Faletau needs finger surgery and misses Ospreys derby, Wales hopes dented
teams.body: Taulupe Faletau will have surgery on a finger injury that surfaced after his Cardiff comeback, his first appearance since March, and he will miss the URC derby at Ospreys. Cardiff hope he can return after the November break, which matters for Wales. Steve Tandy left the 109-cap number eight out of his Nations Championship squad, but said he would not rule out an international return if Faletau shows he can stay fit.

lead.why: A fresh injury to Wales's most capped current-era number eight, with direct consequences for the Nations Championship picture.

teams.heading: Contepomi recalls captain Montoya and Kremer for London camp; Ruiz, Oviedo injured
teams.body: Felipe Contepomi has named a 33-man squad for the London camp, which Americas Rugby News reported midweek as his strongest roster of the year. Captain Julián Montoya returns after missing the recent home matches against Australia and South Africa, and Marcos Kremer is back in the pack. Hooker Ignacio Ruiz and No. 8 Joaquín Oviedo are injured and absent. The squad assembles in London from Monday, and Contepomi will confirm his November squad after the three-day camp, ahead of the tour to Ireland, Italy and France.

lead.why: It is a new men's national squad story that has not yet been run, and it is about Argentina's own roster rather than another team's injury.

teams.heading: Taniela Tupou and Tom Hooper return to Wallabies' 33-man spring squad
teams.body: According to the Guardian, coach Les Kiss's 33-man spring squad includes Taniela Tupou and Tom Hooper, who play club rugby in France and England and were unavailable against New Zealand because those Tests fell outside World Rugby's global player release period. Both delivered crucial bench roles in the win over back-to-back World Cup champions South Africa. Len Ikitau is also back from injury, while Tom Lambert joins Teddy Wilson as a new face.

lead.why: It is the Wallabies' own squad news, and it adds a different angle to the Wilson call-up already covered: the return of Tupou and Hooper after missing the All Blacks Tests.

teams.heading: Japan's highest-ever world ranking stands at No. 7, set in 2019
teams.body: Japan's best world ranking ever reached is No. 7, set in 2019. In the log they are 10 of 12 after three matches: one win, two defeats, no draws. Across those three games they have scored 62 points and conceded 88, a points difference of minus 26. Their last result was a 28-34 defeat to Fiji, and the next fixture is Wales.

teams.heading: Captain Ardie Savea among seven more All Blacks unavailable for Europe
teams.body: Captain Ardie Savea is among seven further All Blacks listed as unavailable for the Nations Championship campaign in Europe, according to SA Rugby Magazine, with shoulder trouble sidelining him. The list also covers Ruben Love, Luke Jacobson, Caleb Clarke, Billy Proctor, Ollie Norris and Tamaiti Williams, on top of the four players already ruled out. Richie Mo’unga, who missed both Bledisloe Cup Tests with a calf tear, has not yet been ruled out.

lead.why: It is a new development on the All Blacks' injury list, with the captain among the newly unavailable players, and it is a national-team story rather than a league, retired-player or club item.

teams.heading: Andre Esterhuizen's foot injury a worry for Erasmus' Springboks squad
teams.body: Sharks captain Andre Esterhuizen was forced off after 52 seconds of Friday's URC match at Cardiff, landing awkwardly on his right foot after an aerial contest and unable to stand on it. Jaco Williams replaced him. Coach Rassie Erasmus is expected to announce his squad for the Nations Championship tour in the coming week, and Esterhuizen, who alternates between backline and loose forward duty, has been described as a vital cog in the Springboks' machine.

lead.why: Planet Rugby's report on Esterhuizen's foot injury is a new Springboks angle ahead of Erasmus's squad announcement, not a retelling of the Sharks result.
